findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Run `find_referencing_symbols` (or equivalent LSP query) on `BindingStore.set_baseline` and separately grep for the string `set_baseline` across the repo to produce a complete, symbol-graph-derived call-site inventory; add `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/classify/test_multipass_stateful.py` (lines 89, 109) to the Files section and confirm its behavior is consistent with A1's changed semantics.
evidence: Plan inventory: '`reconcile._advance_baselines` begins at `reconcile.py:520`', '`apply_inbound_records.py:257-260`', '`BindingStore.seed_baselines_from_snapshot` begins at `binding_store.py:468`' — no mention of classify tests.
Files listed: `binding_store.py`, `reconcile.py`, `apply_inbound_records.py`, `test_binding_baseline.py`, `test_reconcile_idempotency.py` — `test_multipass_stateful.py` absent.

Grep result: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/classify/test_multipass_stateful.py:89: store.set_baseline(store.get_local_id(jira_key), snapshot()[jira_key])` and `test_multipass_stateful.py:109: store2.set_baseline('loc-arch', snapshot()['REB-2'])` — two direct structural call sites not covered by plan inventory.
findings.finding: `set_baseline` call-site inventory omits `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/classify/test_multipass_stateful.py`, which has two direct structural calls to `store.set_baseline(...)` at lines 89 and 109. This file is not listed in the plan's Files section nor mentioned in its call-site narrative. A1 changes `set_baseline` behavior (adds field filtering, equality guard, early return), making this an affected reference site.
findings.location: "Implemented behavior and call sites" section and "Files" section
scenarios: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/classify/test_multipass_stateful.py` calls `set_baseline` directly at lines 89 and 109. If the changed filtering/equality behavior caused any unexpected side effect in these test scenarios (e.g., a baseline not being written due to the equality guard when the test expects it to be), this file would surface the regression — but only if it was identified as an affected site and verified as part of A1's coverage audit.

The plan's AC states 'the complete repository suite is green: make test passed with 8,519 passed' — this implicitly covers the omitted file, but the call-site inventory was not symbol-graph-derived; a future narrower change to `set_baseline` could miss this file again if the inventory is reused as a template.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add at least a debug-level log line (or a counter metric) in set_baseline when the guard fires (skips the write) so operators can verify the optimization is active and detect regressions without manual corpus analysis.
evidence: No log, metric, or trace is mentioned anywhere in the plan for the guard's skip or write branch.
The operator-attested packed-cost win is a one-time measurement over a frozen 40-SHA corpus; there is no ongoing signal to detect if the guard stops working correctly in production.
T5b requires: 'New failure points instrumented with a metric/log/trace/alert so operators can see and debug them.'
findings.finding: The new write-when-changed guard introduces a conditional execution path (skip vs. write) that has no associated log statement, metric increment, or trace annotation. Operators cannot observe how frequently the guard fires in production, making it impossible to detect regressions (e.g., guard never firing = always writing) or to validate the packed-cost improvement claim operationally over time.
findings.location: Implemented behavior — binding_store.py:451-466; Acceptance Criteria — operator-attested packed-cost measurement
scenarios: A future refactor accidentally removes the equality guard; without a metric, the regression is invisible until the next manual corpus measurement.

The guard fires unexpectedly frequently (e.g., due to serializer non-determinism producing unequal-but-semantically-identical baselines), causing unexpected write amplification with no observable signal.
findings.suggested_fix: In the early-return branch of set_baseline, emit logger.debug('set_baseline: no change detected for %s, skipping write', key) (or increment a prometheus/statsd counter baseline_write_skipped_total) so the guard's behavior is observable in production logs.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the specific test function(s) and observable outcome (e.g. 'serialized bytes unchanged after inbound-adopt when baseline is unmodified') that prove the inbound-adopt path (`apply_inbound_records.py:257-260`) behaves correctly under A1's write-when-changed guard.
evidence: 'retains its existing focused coverage' is effort/process-framed, not outcome-framed: it describes preserving test count, not what the inbound-adopt path is proved to do under A1's new guarded behavior.
No test name or file path is cited for the inbound-adopt half of this criterion, unlike every other AC which names a specific test function or command.
findings.finding: AC7's second clause — 'the inbound-adopt path retains its existing focused coverage' — states no specific observable outcome and names no test, making it impossible to evaluate independently of a green `make test` sweep.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'Repeated seed_baselines_from_snapshot input preserves serialized bytes, and the inbound-adopt path retains its existing focused coverage.'
scenarios: An agent verifying A1 completeness cannot independently confirm the inbound-adopt path behaves correctly under the guard without knowing which test exercises it and what observable outcome it asserts.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'the inbound-adopt path retains its existing focused coverage' with a statement such as: 'The inbound-adopt path (`apply_inbound_records.py:257-260`) is covered by `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_reconcile_idempotency.py` (or the named unit test in `test_binding_baseline.py`) and produces byte-identical baseline entries when the inbound value is unchanged, proved by [test-function-name].'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC (or expand the unit-test AC) that names the five mirrored fields, asserts they are excluded from the stored baseline, and verifies that non-mirrored fields are preserved — so the filtering behavior has a covering criterion.
evidence: 'set_baseline now filters the five mirrored fields' — Outcome, first sentence
No AC references field-filtering correctness, field count, or which five fields are involved
The unit test file test_binding_baseline.py is listed but its coverage of the filtering behavior is not described
findings.finding: The Outcome section names 'filtering the five mirrored fields' as a distinct implemented behavior, but no Acceptance Criterion verifies which fields are filtered, how many, or that the filtering is correct. This is a described deliverable with no covering criterion.
findings.location: Outcome section ('filters the five mirrored fields'); Acceptance Criteria section (no corresponding AC)
scenarios: A bug in the field-filtering logic (e.g., filtering the wrong fields, or filtering six instead of five) would not be caught by any named AC
A reviewer cannot verify the filtering behavior from the AC set alone
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC such as: 'set_baseline strips exactly the five mirrored fields [list them] from the stored entry and retains all other keys; proved by test_mirrored_fields_excluded_from_baseline in test_binding_baseline.py.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit rollback statement for A1 — e.g., 'Reverting commit 750a56b3 is sufficient to restore stamp writes; existing cache artifacts with or without the stamp are forward- and backward-compatible because no production reader was ever present (verified by grep AC).'
evidence: T4 requires: 'The remedy is an explicit rollback/back-out plan or expand-contract — acknowledgement alone is insufficient'
The plan acknowledges inertness of old keys but does not state what a rollback of A1 entails or whether it is safe
The grep AC confirms no production reader, which reduces risk, but rollback procedure is still unspecified
findings.finding: The plan removes writes of baseline_advanced_at from set_baseline (a data-shape change) and defers cleanup of existing cached artifacts to the parent epic, but provides no explicit rollback or back-out path for A1 itself — only the acknowledgement that old keys are inert.
findings.location: Implemented behavior section ('Historical serialized stamp keys are inert; cleanup of cache history/current cache artifacts belongs to the parent epic rollout and rewrite, not to a new production reader or migration in A1.')
scenarios: If A1 must be reverted (e.g., due to an unforeseen downstream issue in the parent epic), the operator has no documented procedure for rolling back — specifically, whether reverting the code change is sufficient or whether cache artifacts need remediation
findings.suggested_fix: Under Implemented behavior or a new Rollback section, add: 'Rollback: revert commit 750a56b3b004f3c3f4cc1b456d3c56bd7809b87d. No cache migration is required in either direction because baseline_advanced_at has no production reader. Cache files written after rollback will resume stamping; files written before revert that lack the stamp remain valid for the same reason.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly whether set_baseline's check-then-write is safe under concurrent reconciler execution (e.g., confirm the reconciler is single-threaded per binding store, or add a lock/atomic CAS around the equality check and write).
evidence: 'filters the five mirrored fields, preserves keys whose value is None, returns early when the stored baseline is equal, and never reads the clock or writes baseline_advanced_at'
No mention of a lock, transaction, or single-threaded execution guarantee anywhere in the plan.
The reconciler is stateful and the plan lists multiple call sites (reconcile.py:520, apply_inbound_records.py:257-260), meaning concurrent adoption and advance-baseline paths could interleave.
findings.finding: The set_baseline guard performs an equality check on the stored baseline and then conditionally writes — a check-then-act (TOCTOU) pattern. The plan is silent on whether concurrent reconciler invocations are prevented or whether the in-memory check+assign is protected by a lock/transaction, leaving a potential race window where two concurrent passes both observe the old value, both decide to write, and one clobbers the other's update.
findings.location: Implemented behavior — binding_store.py:451-466 (set_baseline filtering, equality comparison, early return, changed-value assignment)
scenarios: Two concurrent reconciler passes over the same binding entry both read the current baseline, both compare it as changed, both proceed past the guard, and the second write silently drops the first write's update.
An at-least-once delivery mechanism re-drives the inbound-adopt path concurrently with a scheduled advance-baselines pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-line comment or plan note confirming the reconciler holds a per-store lock or runs in a single-threaded event loop, so reviewers can verify the TOCTOU window is closed by the caller's concurrency model rather than by set_baseline itself.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define a minimum retirement trigger for stale `baseline_advanced_at` keys (e.g., stripped on read in set_baseline/load, or confirm the parent epic story is a hard dependency with a deadline), so the RETIRE path is bounded even if the parent epic is delayed.
evidence: 'Historical serialized stamp keys are inert; cleanup of cache history/current cache artifacts belongs to the parent epic rollout and rewrite'

The RETIRE/cleanup path is acknowledged as out-of-scope for A1 but no interim guard (e.g., a read-time strip on load) is specified to prevent the stale keys from persisting indefinitely if the parent epic is delayed or cancelled.
findings.finding: The RETIRE lifecycle for stale `baseline_advanced_at` keys that already exist in deployed cache files is explicitly deferred to a separate story (`deeb-89c1-1080-4690`). As specified, A1 leaves an unbounded accumulation of inert keys in any cache artifact written before this change, with no expiry, migration trigger, or TTL defined in this plan.
findings.location: Implemented behavior section — 'Historical serialized stamp keys are inert; cleanup of cache history/current cache artifacts belongs to the parent epic rollout and rewrite, not to a new production reader or migration in A1.'
scenarios: The parent epic (`deeb-89c1-1080-4690`) is deprioritized or cancelled, leaving stale baseline_advanced_at keys in all pre-A1 cache files permanently.
A tool that introspects bindings.json for schema conformance starts failing on the inert keys because no cleanup ever ran.
